Conclusion

Role-based action authorization is a common requirement in enterprise SAP applications. In RAP, this can be implemented cleanly by combining PFCG authorization objects, RAP instance authorization, feature control, and backend AUTHORITY-CHECK. 

In this scenario, only users assigned the required authorization through the PFCG role can execute the Manage Status action. Unauthorized users see the action as disabled, while the backend independently validates the authorization before performing the status update.

entry.title: ABAP + MCP: Let AI Do Real Development in Your SAP System
entry.content:
Updated on 30 September 2026 for release 2.7.0. What changed since the earlier revisions is in the project CHANGELOG.

An AI That Works in Your SAP System

A developer opens Claude Desktop and types one sentence: "In DEV, create class ZCL_INVOICE_CHECK in package ZSANDBOX, add a unit test, run it, and show me any ATC findings." Then they watch. The AI searches the system, picks the transport, creates the class, activates it, generates a test include, runs the tests, and reports back with real results from a real SAP system. No copy-pasting between a chatbot and Eclipse.

Twenty seconds of it, as it looks in Claude Desktop:

That is abap-adt-mcp: a free, MIT-licensed, open-source MCP server that gives AI agents full ABAP development capabilities over as many SAP systems as you configure, S/4HANA Cloud and on-premise, with nothing installed inside SAP.

  • Project site, with the films and a three-step setup: https://williansaez.github.io/abap-adt-mcp/
  • Source, issues and documentation: https://github.com/williansaez/abap-adt-mcp
  • Install: npx -y abap-adt-mcp

What Is MCP?

AI assistants like Claude can talk about your SAP system, but they cannot touch it. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard that fixes this: an MCP server is a small program on your own machine that exposes "tools" the AI can call, always with your approval. Plug in abap-adt-mcp and the AI can develop ABAP. It works with any client that speaks MCP: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, VS Code with GitHub Copilot, the Copilot CLI, Cursor, Cline, Windsurf and others.

Under the hood there is no magic. ADT, the protocol your Eclipse installation already uses, is a set of REST services under /sap/bc/adt, and this server calls them through the abap-adt-api library by marcellourbani. If ADT works against your system today, this works too. Everything runs on your machine: no add-on, no transport, no Basis project.

What Can It Do?

Before: you ask an AI about ABAP, it guesses from training data, and you paste code back and forth into Eclipse or SAP GUI. After: the AI reads the real object from your system, edits it, activates it and tests it, while you supervise.

Fix a bug. "Method CALCULATE_TAX in ZCL_BILLING dumps on empty input. Find it and fix it." The AI finds the class, reads the method, picks the transport, replaces exactly the lines that need to change, activates, runs the unit tests and shows you the diff. The chain is searchObject → getMethodSource → resolveTransport → editObjectSource with activate=true → unitTestRun → objectDiff. Locking and unlocking happen inside the write tool, and a stale edit is refused because the server re-reads the source from SAP before every replacement.

Quality pass. "Run ATC on my package and apply the safe quickfixes." The AI runs the check with createAtcRun, totals the findings by priority with atcSummary, then applies the deterministic fixes with atcQuickfixProposals and atcApplyQuickfix. The same flow ships as the built-in prompt fix-atc, which re-runs ATC until priority 1 and 2 are clean.

Explore across systems. "Where is table ZORDERS used, and show me the last 10 rows in QAS." That is whereUsed on one system and runQuery on another, in one conversation, because every tool takes a destination parameter. "Is ZCL_ORDER_SERVICE ready for ABAP Cloud?" is apiReleaseState: it checks every SAP object the class references against SAP's official cloudification repository and, since 2.6.0, reports each object's standing under the SAP API Policy.

Create data end-to-end. "Create table ZTRAVEL_LOG with fields ID, DESTINATION and TRAVEL_DATE, and insert a first entry: Berlin, today." The AI creates and activates the table, then hands a small INSERT to runSnippet, which wraps it in a temporary class, runs it and deletes the class again. Finally it reads the row back with runQuery. You approve every write.

173 tools in 16 toolsets

ToolsetToolsExamples
Destinations, health & session6listSystems, healthcheck, systemProfile
Source code16getObjectSource, editObjectSource, setMethodSource, objectDiff
Objects & navigation27searchObject, createObject, packageTree, whereUsed, grepPackage
Transports18resolveTransport, transportUnifiedDiff, transportRelease
Syntax & code analysis16syntaxCheckCode, apiReleaseState, runSnippet, codeCompletion
Unit tests4unitTestRun, createTestInclude
ATC14createAtcRun, atcSummary, atcApplyQuickfix
Data access & DDIC10runQuery, tableContents, getDomainProperties
Runtime errors3dumps, dumpDetails
Discovery & metadata7loadTypes, adtDiscovery
Refactoring8renameExecute, extractMethodExecute, changePackageExecute
RAP generation8rapGenGenerate, rapGenPublishService
Business services4fetchServiceDetails, publishServiceBinding
abapGit10gitPullRepo, stageRepo, pushRepo
Debugger13debuggerSetBreakpoints, debuggerVariables
Traces9tracesHitList, tracesStatements

The full reference, generated from the live server with a "read-only · writes · destructive" legend on every tool, is docs/TOOLS.md. Six workflows also travel as MCP prompts (create-object, safe-edit, review-transport, fix-atc, clean-core-check, debug-dump); in Claude Code they appear as slash commands.

Set It Up in 10 Minutes

Prerequisites

  • Node.js 22.12 or newer (22 or 24 LTS) from nodejs.org; npm and npx come with it. On a managed laptop the ticket to IT is one line: "Please install Node.js LTS".
  • A Chromium browser (Chrome, Edge or Brave) for the browser login.
  • An ABAP system reachable via ADT. On S/4HANA Cloud your user needs the developer business role (SAP_BR_DEVELOPER in the standard delivery). On-premise, /sap/bc/adt must be active in transaction SICF. If Eclipse ADT connects, you are set.
  • A client that supports MCP. This guide was tested with Claude Desktop and Claude Code.

Start with a development system.

Step 1: Describe your system

Create the folder .abap-adt-mcp in your home directory and a file systems.json inside it. One S/4HANA Cloud tenant with browser SSO, writes limited to Z* packages:

{
  "DEV": {
    "url": "https://myXXXXXX.s4hana.cloud.sap",
    "client": "080",
    "authType": "sso",
    "default": true,
    "policy": { "allowedPackages": ["Z*"] }
  }
}

One system is enough to start. Production and on-premise entries, with a read-only policy, secrets taken from the environment and a corporate CA, are step 4 of the README's Setup section, for after your first success.

Step 2: Register with your AI client

The package is on npm as abap-adt-mcp; npx fetches it. Nothing to clone, nothing to build. Every entry passes the server two settings: where systems.json is, and MCP_TOOLSETS=focused, which publishes the 114 everyday development tools instead of all 173 so the tool schemas do not eat the chat's context. Drop it when you need the debugger, traces, abapGit, RAP or refactoring.

Claude Code, one line:

claude mcp add -s user abap-adt-mcp -e SAP_SYSTEMS_FILE=$HOME/.abap-adt-mcp/systems.json -e MCP_TOOLSETS=focused -- npx -y abap-adt-mcp

Claude Desktop, no terminal needed: Settings → Developer → Edit Config opens the folder that holds claude_desktop_config.json; open it in Notepad or any editor and paste the block below, replacing <you> with your user name (macOS: /Users/<you>/.abap-adt-mcp/systems.json; the forward slashes in the Windows path are deliberate). If Settings has no Developer tab, your Claude Desktop is managed by IT: ask them to add the entry. Then quit and reopen the app; the config is read only at start.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "abap-adt-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "abap-adt-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "SAP_SYSTEMS_FILE": "C:/Users/<you>/.abap-adt-mcp/systems.json",
        "MCP_TOOLSETS": "focused"
      }
    }
  }
}

The same JSON works in Cursor, Cline and other hosts that read an mcpServers map; VS Code names the map servers. docs/HOSTS.md has the per-host form. If the server never appears in the host, the README's Troubleshooting section names the log file to read.

Step 3: Say hello

Restart your client and build trust step by step:

  1. "List my SAP systems and run a healthcheck." Confirms the connection.
  2. "Log in to DEV and show me the source of class CL_ABAP_CHAR_UTILITIES." First real read; the browser window for SSO appears here.
  3. Then the full workflow from the top of this post: create a class, add a unit test, run it, check ATC.

Bonus: let the agent do the installation

Claude Code users have the shortest path. The repository is a plugin marketplace, so two commands register the server and load the two skills that ship with it: one teaches the model how to develop ABAP with these tools, the other walks it through setup and a first health check.

/plugin marketplace add williansaez/abap-adt-mcp
/plugin install abap-adt-mcp@abap-adt-mcp

In any client that can run commands or edit files, Steps 1 and 2 can be delegated too. The prompt that works best names the source of truth, the destination, and where to stop:

"Set up the abap-adt-mcp MCP server for me, following the Setup section of https://github.com/williansaez/abap-adt-mcp#setup. Check that Node.js 22.12 or newer is installed. Create ~/.abap-adt-mcp/systems.json with one destination called DEV: url https://myXXXXXX.s4hana.cloud.sap, client 080, SSO authentication, default, allowed packages Z*. Register the server in this client under the key abap-adt-mcp, started with npx -y abap-adt-mcp, with SAP_SYSTEMS_FILE pointing at that file and MCP_TOOLSETS=focused. Do not put any password in the file. Tell me when I have to restart the client."

Two things stay with you: restarting the client, and the first browser login for SSO destinations.

Is This Safe? Read Before Pointing It at PRD

An AI with write access to SAP deserves a straight answer:

  • Guard rails are enforced by the server, not by the chat client. Each destination can carry a policy block (readOnly, allowedPackages, deniedTables, deniedTools, allowedTransports), checked before every SAP call, whatever the host approves. Add "policy": { "readOnly": true } to any productive or test system and the server refuses every write there, whatever the model is asked. Refusals reach the model as a policyDenied error naming the gate.
  • Business data stays closed by default. runQuery and tableContents are refused until a destination's policy opens them (allowFreeSql or allowDataPreview), and values come back exactly as SAP sent them.
  • Every tool carries MCP read-only/destructive annotations, so your client can ask for approval on risky calls. Review before approving: deleteObject, transportRelease, transportDelete, setObjectSource, editObjectSource, runSnippet, pushRepo.
  • The AI can only do what your SAP user can do. Every call reaches SAP as the user of the destination, with that user's authorizations; the server removes no SAP check. Point it at development systems and use a least-privilege user.
  • What leaves your machine. The result of every tool call you approve (source, table rows where opened, dumps, ATC findings) goes to your MCP host and from there to the model provider under the host's own data terms. The server sends nothing anywhere else: no telemetry, no update checks.
  • Credential hygiene is built in. Four logon modes: browser SSO (the default, like Eclipse), basic, OAuth client credentials for S/4HANA Cloud technical users, and a headless sso2 mode for environments that already authenticate a named user through SNC; details in docs/AUTH.md. ${env:VAR} keeps secrets out of systems.json, a world-readable file with inline passwords is refused at startup, TLS verification cannot be switched off for everything at once, and reentranceTicket is disabled by default.
  • Audit trail. Set MCP_AUDIT_FILE and every tool call is appended as one JSON line: tool, destination, duration, outcome, policy gate, redacted arguments.
  • SAP API Policy. The ADT services this server calls are the ones Eclipse uses, and SAP does not publish them on the Business Accelerator Hub. SAP's FAQ on its API Policy calls them internal, for development through the channels SAP endorses, and a third-party MCP server is not among the ones it lists. The same FAQ allows third-party MCP servers in general and says unpublished interfaces are used at your own risk. Ask your SAP contact, keep the server on development and test systems, and read docs/API-POLICY.md for the policy section by section and a conservative configuration.

The write flow in this post was run live on an S/4HANA Public Cloud tenant and on an S/4HANA 2023 on-premise system: package and class created and activated, 2/2 unit tests green, ATC with zero findings, rename and extract-method refactorings with tests staying green, full cleanup afterwards. docs/TESTPLAN.md records every run, including one with GitHub Copilot on Windows 11.

Other SAP + MCP Projects

SAP's official ADT MCP Server ships with ADT for VS Code and Eclipse under the server key abap-adt; this project publishes as abap-adt-mcp with its own tool names, so both can run in the same host, and docs/ROUTING.md maps SAP's tool names to ours. marianfoo's ABAP docs MCP server is a read-only reference library for the ABAP Keyword Documentation and Clean ABAP that never touches a live system; run both, and the docs server answers "how should I write this?" while abap-adt-mcp does it.

Try It, Break It, Tell Me

  • Tool reference: docs/TOOLS.md. Workflows with exact tool sequences: docs/WORKFLOWS.md. Every option and policy: docs/CONFIGURATION.md. Authentication: docs/AUTH.md.
  • Issues and pull requests are welcome at https://github.com/williansaez/abap-adt-mcp.

I would genuinely like to hear how it goes: what works, what breaks, what is missing. And a question for the comments: what is the first thing you would ask an AI to do in your DEV system?

Thank you for reading!

This post was assisted by GenAI. Every claim was reviewed, tested against a live system, and validated by me.

entry.title: ABAP Sessions at Devtoberfest 2026
entry.content:
🔥Check out the ABAP sessions at SAP TechEd 2026! ‌‌🔥

Hey Everyone! 

From September 21 to October 18, 2026, Devtoberfest from SAP is back 🎉, and so is our dedicated lineup of insightful ABAP sessions! This year, we’re exploring what’s new and what’s next in ABAP, with a strong focus on Agentic AI, ABAP Cloud innovations, custom code migration, and developer productivity.

Key event info for 2026:

  • 📅Dates: September 21 – October 18, 2026
  • 🔁 Tradition continues: Every Monday during Devtoberfest is ABAP Day🟢! 
  • 📺 Where: All sessions livestreamed or premiered on the SAP Developers YouTube channel 
  • 📚 Session catalog: Explore the full session line-up in the SAP Community events area: Devtoberfest
  • 📅 Event calendar: Devtoberfest Calendar | Devtoberfest Schedule 

🎮 Don't forget the fun: Join the Devtoberfest gamification activities (Type: Activity) and earn points! See the Leaderboard.

 Following last year’s ABAP session overview, this blog brings all the ABAP sessions at Devtoberfest 2026 together in one place. Whether you are working with classic ABAP, exploring ABAP Cloud, building extensions on SAP BTP, or simply looking to discover what’s new, there should be plenty to explore. So, let’s take a look at what’s on the agenda and find the sessions that are right for you!

Find the compact overview of ABAP sessions at Devtoberfest 2026 below. Session details are provided in the next section. Expect plenty demos and opportunities to interact with SAP experts and fellow developers!

📅 [CW 39] WEEK 1 – 🟢 September 21, 2026

  • 11:00am CEST | ABAP Language Innovations: What's New
  • 01:00am CEST | S/4HANA Custom Development – What happens in case of errors in BAPIs or RAP BOs?
  • 03:00pm CEST | What's new with draft handling in RAP?

📅 [CW 40] WEEK 2 – 🟢 September 28, 2026

  • 09:00am CEST | Agentic Loop with Joule for Developers and ADT MCP Server
  • 11:00am CEST | How to build an application job in SAP BAIP, ABAP environment
  • 01:00pm CEST | News from Custom Code Migration: ECC to SAP S/4HANA Powered by Agentic AI
  • 03:00pm CEST | ABAP Development Tools for VS Code

📅 [CW 41] WEEK 3 – 🟢 October 5, 2026

  • 08:00am CEST | Always in Sync – Field-level and event-driven side effects for reactive UIs in RAP
  • 11:00am CEST | How to implement business AI capabilities in ABAP Cloud
  • 03:00pm CEST | Updates on Embedded Analytics in ABAP Cloud for Developers

📅 [CW 42] WEEK 4 – 🟢 October 12, 2026

  • 11:00am CEST | ABAP CDS Associations & Joins
  • 01:00pm CEST | Developing and managing authorizations for business users in SAP BAIP, ABAP environment
  • 03:00pm CEST | SAP ABAP Environment – How to build partner solutions and get them certified
  • 05:00pm CEST | ABAP AI SDK powered by ISLM - How to implement your own AI use cases in ABAP

Session Details

◈ Week 1: Sep 21 – Sep 27, 2026

ABAP Language Innovations: What's New
Discover the latest innovations in the ABAP language and see how they simplify everyday development. This session covers new features such as DELETE DUPLICATES, generic structures, support for cyclic references, boolean expressions, and CamelCase handling in CALL TRANSFORMATION. Learn the motivation behind these enhancements, how they work, and how you can leverage them to write cleaner, more expressive, and more robust ABAP code. 
Speakers:  Kilian Kilger (SAP), Cedric Becker (SAP), Kai Müller (SAP), Niko Haas (SAP)
Schedule: 21 September 2026, 11:00am – 12:00pm CEST


S/4HANA Custom Development - What happens in case of errors in BAPIs or RAP BOs?
In this session, we will discuss common processing scenarios from customer projects, including event-driven processing, API integrations, Application Jobs, and user-triggered mass processing in Fiori. Based on modern ABAP, RAP, Fiori, Application Jobs, Application Logs, and Clean Core principles, we will explore a common approach for process execution, error handling, resume capabilities, monitoring, and business-oriented mass processing. 
The result is a consistent pattern for building restartable, transparent, and user-friendly business processes while keeping business logic separated from technical process orchestration
Speakers: Marcel Hermanns (Brandeis Consulting)
Schedule: 21 September 2026, 1:00pm – 2:00pm CEST


What's new with draft handling in RAP?
In this session we will show the two new concepts that are available with draft.
With collaborative draft it is possible that several users work on the same item which was not possible so far in a draft enabled RAP business object.
And with draft scope it is possible to build two draft enabled RAP business objects such that one business object depends on the other. When an instance of the principal (independent) draft BO is set to edit mode and thus set to draft, all related instances of the dependent draft BO are set to draft as well.
Speakers:  André Fischer (SAP)
Schedule: 21 September 2026, 3:00pm – 4:00pm CEST


Bring AI into Your ABAP Applications with ISLM: Build, Integrate, and Consume AI Natively 
Explore how ISLM provides an ABAP-native foundation to consume SAP-delivered AI scenarios and build custom AI solutions directly within SAP S/4HANA—without additional middleware. See how the ABAP AI SDK, powered by ISLM, enables seamless AI integration into ABAP applications and business processes.
Learn how ISLM supports classical AI and Generative AI, enabling governed integration, consumption, and lifecycle management, while also supporting low-code AI development.
Get a sneak peek at Tabular AI and the latest capabilities, including System-Triggered Agents, laying the foundation for the autonomous enterprise. 
Speakers: Abhishek Mishra (SAP),  Priti Dhingra (SAP)
Schedule: 24 September 2026, 9:00am – 10:00pm CEST

 

◈ Week 2: Sep 28 – Oct 4, 2026


Agentic Loop with Joule for Developers and ADT MCP Server
Code smarter as Joule for Developers brings AI into everyday ABAP work. Learn how agentic flows work in VS Code and ADT using third party orchestrators as side-by-side solution bringing it to even lower releases. Learn how ABAP MCP servers and the additional method add tools, guardrails, and review loops.
Speakers: Rushikesh Nagle (SAP), Sanjay Porwal (SAP)
Schedule: 28 September 2026, 9:00am – 10:00pm CEST


How to build an application job in SAP BAIP, ABAP environment
Using the new application job interface IF_APJ_RT_RUN the development of application jobs has become easier and improved scheduling capabilities have been made available. 
Speakers:  André Fischer (SAP)
Schedule: 28 September 2026, 11:00am – 12:00pm CEST


News from Custom Code Migration: ECC to SAP S/4HANA Powered by Agentic AI
Migrating custom code during an ECC to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition system conversion can be a complex and time-consuming journey. In this session, you will learn how ABAP AI capabilities in SAP Joule for Developers, the S/4HANA Custom Code Migration agent, and the latest enhancements in custom code management tools help accelerate and automate custom code migration. 
Speakers:  Olga Dolinskaja (SAP), Thomas Fiedler (SAP)
Schedule: 28 September 2026, 01:00pm – 11:30am CEST
 


ABAP Development Tools for VS Code
Get to know the ADT extension and its capabilities for AI-based ABAP development.
Speakers:  Wolfgang Wöhrle (SAP), Ünal Akkaya (SAP)
Schedule: 28 September 2026, 4:00pm – 5:00pm CEST

◈ Week 3: Oct 5 – Oct 11, 2026


Always in Sync – Field-level and event-driven side effects for reactive UIs in RAP
In this session we will show an easy way to start an asynchronous process using BGPF (e.g. the calculation of an inventory entry) and an easy way how to update the UI with the result of the calculation using Event driven side effects when the asynchronous process has finished.
Speakers:  André Fischer (SAP)
Schedule: 5 October 2026, 8:00am – 9:00am CEST


How to implement business AI capabilities in ABAP Cloud
Learn how to embed business AI capabilities in your ABAP Cloud application built with RAP and how to integrate it with Joule. 
Speakers:  Fabian Fellhauer (SAP)
Schedule: 5 October 2026, 11:00am – 12:00pm CEST
Blog post: 

  • Business AI in ABAP Cloud – A Strategic Overview (Part 1) 
  • Business AI in ABAP Cloud - Embedding AI with the ABAP AI SDK (Part 2) 


Updates on Embedded Analytics in ABAP Cloud for Developers
In this demo session, we will show you how to develop embedded analytical applications using ABAP Development tools and generator wizards. We will touch the development of Multidimensional Analysis, Review Booklets as well as developing custom hierarchies. We will also give an outlook on planned enhancements.
Speakers:  Timo Schaaf (SAP), Andreas Riehl (SAP)
Schedule: 5 October 2026, 3:00pm – 4:00pm CEST

◈ Week 4: Oct 12 – Oct 18, 2026


CDS Associations & Joins
Overview and fundamentals of CDS associations and join techniques with a focus on how to use them effectively in real-world. It highlights common pitfalls and design patterns that directly impact query behavior, automatic optimizations and runtime efficiency on SAP HANA.
Speakers:  Hermann Gahm (SAP), Robert Werlich (SAP)
Schedule: 12 October 2026, 11:00am – 12:00pm CEST


Developing and managing authorizations for business users in SAP BAIP, ABAP environment
In this presentation, we will show you the development and use of customer-specific authorization objects in the SAP BAIP, ABAP environment with the innovation delivered in release 2608 for maintaining restriction types at the IAM application level.
Speakers: André Fischer (SAP)
Schedule: 12 October 2026, 1:00pm – 2:00pm CEST


SAP ABAP Environment – How to build partner solutions and get them certified
The SAP BTP ABAP Environment offers partner different ways for developing and delivering ABAP based solutions to their customer. This session focuses on an overview about the delivery options, customer like testing before delivery as well as on the certification options and how to get your partner solution certified.
Speakers:  Prashanth Kalur (SAP), Ronny Pahlke (SAP)
Schedule: 12 October 2026, 3:00pm – 4:00pm CEST


ABAP AI SDK powered by ISLM - How to implement your own AI use cases in ABAP
Empower yourself to build your own GenAI use cases in ABAP. The ABAP AI SDK powered by ISLM brings the key capabilities of SAP AI Core directly into ABAP without leaving your ABAP stack.
Speakers: Matthias Iacsa (SAP)
Schedule: 12 October 2026, 5:00pm – 6:00pm CEST


💡I also strongly recommend checking out the full event agenda or session schedule for many more interesting sessions, including:

  • 🟠 Intelligent App Development at Scale: SAP Fiori Elements + ABAP Development Tools for VS Code
  • 🟡 An AI Skeptic’s Conversion: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love AI
  • 🟡 Build Your Reputation: Harness AI for Blogging (and still stay human)

 ____________________________________________________________________________________________

Ready to see what's new? Join us throughout Devtoberfest and discover the latest ABAP innovations, AI capabilities, and development practices in action.

If you want to get a head start, take a look at the replays from SAP's Devtoberfest 2025 and SAP TechEd Virtual 2025 for even more ABAP insights.

entry.title: Designing a configurable REST dispatcher in ABAP
entry.content:
How can an ABAP application expose multiple HTTP operations without putting all its routing decisions into one large handler?

I developed an approach called ABAP Dynamic REST. It separates the HTTP entry point, endpoint configuration, and operation-specific ABAP logic. This article walks through that separation and the design decisions it introduces.

The excerpts below follow the active dispatcher read from an ECC sandbox on 11 September 2026. Customer namespace names have been replaced consistently with ZCL_AGENT_DISPATCHER, ZAGENT_ENDPOINTS and ZIF_AGENT_HANDLER. They are excerpts, not a complete transport or an authorization framework. The combined, renamed code was syntax-checked in a standalone harness on that system; the runtime scenarios below remain tests to perform.

The architecture

The HTTP entry point is implemented by ZCL_AGENT_DISPATCHER through IF_HTTP_EXTENSION. The dispatcher resolves a request to a handler using the endpoint registry, ZAGENT_ENDPOINTS.

Figure 1. Registry-driven dispatch. This is an explanatory diagram, not a screenshot of a running SAP system.

A registry entry supplies the route and HTTP method, the implementing class and method, an activation flag, and an optional authorization object. Handlers implement a shared interface to receive the request and response references; a base class can supply common behavior.

The distinction matters: configuration selects behavior that has already been implemented. Adding a new business operation still requires developing, testing and deploying its handler.

1. Define the route cache

These declarations belong to the dispatcher. The hashed key contains both path and HTTP method; the registry also has a client key. The fields below are the routing projection, not the complete dictionary table definition.

TYPES:
  BEGIN OF ty_endpoint_cache,
    endpoint_path TYPE char100,
    http_method   TYPE char10,
    class_name    TYPE seoclsname,
    method_name   TYPE seocpdname,
    auth_object   TYPE xuobject,
  END OF ty_endpoint_cache,
  tt_endpoint_cache TYPE HASHED TABLE OF ty_endpoint_cache
                    WITH UNIQUE KEY endpoint_path http_method.

CLASS-DATA gt_endpoint_cache TYPE tt_endpoint_cache.
CLASS-DATA gv_cache_loaded TYPE abap_bool.

Following a request

The dispatcher reads the request method and path. When its class cache is not loaded, it reads active registry entries into a hashed table keyed by endpoint path and HTTP method.

It first looks for an exact path/method key. In the current sandbox version, the subsequent loop also uses equality, not substring matching. The selected class is instantiated, cast to the handler interface and initialized. The authorization hook is then called before method execution; a handler that does not implement the interface is rejected.

Figure 2. Overview of the routing stages. The excerpts below specify the current exact-match and fail-closed interface policy. OPTIONS requests return before route resolution.

An unresolved route returns HTTP 404. A denied configured authorization check returns 403. Class-creation or handler exceptions are caught and returned as 500 responses. Successful response construction depends on the handler.

2. Read the request and resolve a route

Excerpt from IF_HTTP_EXTENSION~HANDLE_REQUEST. Its local variables and outer exception handler are omitted here. OPTIONS returns before loading the registry; unresolved routes are returned as 404 by the surrounding method.

lv_method = server->request->get_method( ).

  IF lv_method = 'OPTIONS'.
    server->response->set_status( code = 200 reason = 'OK' ).
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  lv_path = server->request->get_header_field( '~path_info' ).

  IF gv_cache_loaded = abap_false.
    load_cache( ).
  ENDIF.

  resolve_handler(
      EXPORTING
        iv_path   = lv_path
        iv_method = lv_method
      IMPORTING
        ev_class_name  = lv_class_name
        ev_method_name = lv_method_name
        ev_auth_object = lv_auth_object
        rv_found       = lv_found ).

Why cache the registry?

Reading the registry into a class-level cache separates routing from repeated configuration reads. However, configuration changes and cache visibility must be considered together.

The dispatcher exposes REFRESH_CACHE, which clears its loaded flag. The next relevant load rebuilds the cache. This is not, by itself, evidence of immediate invalidation across all active sessions. A deployment should define how configuration changes become visible and test that behavior.

3. Load active entries and invalidate the cache

ZAGENT_ENDPOINTS is the renamed registry table. It must exist with the matching DDIC fields. Open SQL applies normal client handling. REFRESH_CACHE clears the flag; LOAD_CACHE clears and rebuilds the table on the next load. Class data is not a cross-session invalidation mechanism. The INSERT return code is not checked here, so registry uniqueness and duplicate handling deserve explicit tests.

METHOD load_cache.
  DATA: lt_endpoints TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zagent_endpoints,
        ls_endpoint  TYPE zagent_endpoints,
        ls_cache     TYPE ty_endpoint_cache.

  CLEAR gt_endpoint_cache.

  SELECT * FROM zagent_endpoints
    INTO TABLE lt_endpoints
    WHERE is_active = abap_true.

  LOOP AT lt_endpoints INTO ls_endpoint.
    CLEAR ls_cache.
    ls_cache-endpoint_path = ls_endpoint-endpoint_path.
    ls_cache-http_method   = ls_endpoint-http_method.
    ls_cache-class_name    = ls_endpoint-class_name.
    ls_cache-method_name   = ls_endpoint-method_name.
    ls_cache-auth_object   = ls_endpoint-auth_object.
    INSERT ls_cache INTO TABLE gt_endpoint_cache.
  ENDLOOP.

  gv_cache_loaded = abap_true.
ENDMETHOD.

METHOD refresh_cache.
  gv_cache_loaded = abap_false.
ENDMETHOD.

Route matching is a design decision

Earlier versions used substring fallback. This sandbox version uses equality in both paths. Therefore /x/orders/y should not select a registered /orders endpoint merely because it contains that text. The second loop is now largely redundant; I retain it in this excerpt to show the implementation as read rather than silently refactoring it.

For a predictable API contract, test overlapping routes, extra segments and unsupported methods. Despite its name, LV_PATH_UPPER is only assigned; no uppercase conversion occurs. The initial lookup also converts the path to CHAR100, so enforce the route length and normalization policy deliberately. The current implementation reports unresolved path/method combinations as 404 rather than a dedicated 405.

4. Match the path and HTTP method

Both lookup paths use exact equality. A hashed-table loop should not be treated as a route-priority mechanism.

METHOD find_matching_endpoint.
  DATA: ls_cache      TYPE ty_endpoint_cache,
        lv_path_upper TYPE char100.

  rv_found = abap_false.
  lv_path_upper = iv_path.

  READ TABLE gt_endpoint_cache INTO ls_cache
    WITH KEY endpoint_path = lv_path_upper
             http_method   = iv_method.

  IF sy-subrc = 0.
    ev_class_name  = ls_cache-class_name.
    ev_method_name = ls_cache-method_name.
    ev_auth_object = ls_cache-auth_object.
    rv_found = abap_true.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  LOOP AT gt_endpoint_cache INTO ls_cache
    WHERE http_method = iv_method.

    " was CS (substring): a crafted path such as /x/call_function/y could
    " resolve to the /call_function handler. Exact match only.
    IF iv_path = ls_cache-endpoint_path.
      ev_class_name  = ls_cache-class_name.
      ev_method_name = ls_cache-method_name.
      ev_auth_object = ls_cache-auth_object.
      rv_found = abap_true.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDMETHOD.

Authorization belongs at more than one layer

The dispatcher invokes CHECK_AUTHORIZATION whenever the interface cast succeeds, including when IV_AUTH_OBJECT is empty. It is the handler implementation that defines the meaning of that parameter. A failed interface cast or a false result prevents execution and returns 403.

HTTP authentication and route availability do not replace business authorization. Each operation needs checks appropriate to the data or action it exposes. Registry maintenance also deserves controlled access because it determines which class and method can be invoked.

The current dispatcher sets a wildcard CORS origin. That is another deployment choice to assess; it is not a substitute for authentication or authorization. Write operations additionally need defined transaction, locking and rollback behavior.

5. Define the handler contract

The interface shares HTTP references and exposes initialization and authorization. Implementations must actually enforce appropriate permissions; the signature alone does not enforce business access.

interface zif_agent_handler
.

  data MO_REQUEST type ref to IF_HTTP_REQUEST read-only .
  data MO_RESPONSE type ref to IF_HTTP_RESPONSE read-only .
  data MV_BODY type STRING read-only .

  methods INITIALIZE
    importing
      !IO_REQUEST type ref to IF_HTTP_REQUEST
      !IO_RESPONSE type ref to IF_HTTP_RESPONSE .
  methods GET_SUPPORTED_METHODS
    returning
      value(RT_METHODS) type STRING_TABLE .
  methods CHECK_AUTHORIZATION
    importing
      !IV_AUTH_OBJECT type XUOBJECT optional
    preferred parameter IV_AUTH_OBJECT
    returning
      value(RV_AUTHORIZED) type ABAP_BOOL .
endinterface.

6. Instantiate, authorize and invoke the handler

This complete method preserves the current fail-closed interface check and the additional S_DEVELOP activity 02 check for the explicitly listed repository-write methods. The list is not automatic classification of every write. DUMMY fields do not restrict individual object names or packages, so operation-specific checks are still required. Dynamic invocation can fail for invalid method configuration; the catch blocks translate exceptions into HTTP 500. Exposing raw exception text also needs a production error-disclosure review.

METHOD instantiate_and_call.
  DATA: lo_handler    TYPE REF TO object,
        lo_if         TYPE REF TO zif_agent_handler,
        lx_error      TYPE REF TO cx_root,
        lv_error      TYPE string,
        lv_authorized TYPE abap_bool,
        lv_is_write   TYPE abap_bool.

  lv_authorized = abap_true.

  TRY.
      CREATE OBJECT lo_handler TYPE (iv_class_name).

      TRY.
          lo_if ?= lo_handler.
          lo_if->initialize(
            io_request  = io_request
            io_response = io_response ).
        CATCH cx_sy_move_cast_error.
      ENDTRY.

      IF lo_if IS BOUND.
        IF lo_if->check_authorization( iv_auth_object ) = abap_false.
          io_response->set_cdata( '{"status":"error","message":"Not authorized"}' ).
          io_response->set_status( code = 403 reason = 'Forbidden' ).
          io_response->set_content_type( 'application/json' ).
          lv_authorized = abap_false.
        ENDIF.
      ELSE.
*       Fail closed: a handler that does not implement the interface has passed
*       no authorization check; never execute it.
        io_response->set_cdata( '{"status":"error","message":"Handler not authorized"}' ).
        io_response->set_status( code = 403 reason = 'Forbidden' ).
        io_response->set_content_type( 'application/json' ).
        lv_authorized = abap_false.
      ENDIF.

*     Repository writes (code + DDIC) require S_DEVELOP change, not just the
*     display floor enforced in check_authorization.
      IF lv_authorized = abap_true.
        CLEAR lv_is_write.
        CASE iv_method_name.
          WHEN 'HANDLE_WRITE_CODE'
            OR 'HANDLE_PATCH_CLASS_METHOD'
            OR 'HANDLE_PATCH_CLASS_INCLUDE'
            OR 'HANDLE_PATCH_INCL_B64'
            OR 'HANDLE_PATCH_CODE'
            OR 'HANDLE_PATCH_FUNCTION'
            OR 'HANDLE_DELETE_REPO_OBJECT'
            OR 'HANDLE_IMPLEMENT_NOTE_V2'
            OR 'HANDLE_CREATE_TABLE'
            OR 'HANDLE_CREATE_DTEL'
            OR 'HANDLE_CREATE_DOMAIN'.
            lv_is_write = abap_true.
        ENDCASE.

        IF lv_is_write = abap_true.
          AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'S_DEVELOP'
            ID 'DEVCLASS' DUMMY
            ID 'OBJTYPE'  DUMMY
            ID 'OBJNAME'  DUMMY
            ID 'P_GROUP'  DUMMY
            ID 'ACTVT'    FIELD '02'.
          IF sy-subrc <> 0.
            io_response->set_cdata( '{"status":"error","message":"Not authorized for change"}' ).
            io_response->set_status( code = 403 reason = 'Forbidden' ).
            io_response->set_content_type( 'application/json' ).
            lv_authorized = abap_false.
          ENDIF.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.

      IF lv_authorized = abap_true.
        CALL METHOD lo_handler->(iv_method_name).
      ENDIF.

    CATCH cx_sy_create_object_error INTO lx_error.
      io_response->set_cdata( '{"status":"error","message":"Handler class not found"}' ).
      io_response->set_status( code = 500 reason = 'Internal Server Error' ).
      io_response->set_content_type( 'application/json' ).

    CATCH cx_root INTO lx_error.
      lv_error = lx_error->get_text( ).
      REPLACE ALL OCCURRENCES OF '\' IN lv_error WITH '\\'.
      REPLACE ALL OCCURRENCES OF '"' IN lv_error WITH '\"'.
      CONCATENATE '{"status":"error","message":"' lv_error '"}' INTO lv_error.
      io_response->set_cdata( lv_error ).
      io_response->set_status( code = 500 reason = 'Internal Server Error' ).
      io_response->set_content_type( 'application/json' ).
  ENDTRY.
ENDMETHOD.

What I would test

I would test routing separately from each handler's business behavior:

  • Unknown routes and unsupported HTTP methods.
  • Disabled entries before and after cache refresh.
  • Overlapping paths and extra segments that must not resolve through substring matching.
  • Missing handler classes or methods.
  • Interface-cast failures, empty authorization settings, and handler checks that allow and deny access.
  • Handler exceptions and the resulting HTTP response.
  • Operation-specific input validation and business permissions.

These are proposed test scenarios, not a claim that this article demonstrates their execution.

The trade-off

A configurable registry reduces changes to the routing implementation when exposing an existing handler. In exchange, configuration becomes part of the API contract and needs the same care as code: review, change control, documentation and testing.

The pattern is useful to discuss because it makes those responsibilities visible. The important question is not merely whether a request reaches an ABAP method, but whether that route remains understandable, controlled and maintainable as the API grows.

entry.title: XML Upload & Download for Purchase Orders with Deep Structure & SALV ALV Display
entry.content:
Introduction:

In modern SAP applications, business data is often organized in hierarchical relationships rather than simple flat records. Purchase Orders are a typical example, where a single header contains multiple item-level details. Handling such data efficiently requires an appropriate data model that can preserve the relationship between header and item information while also supporting data exchange and user-friendly reporting.

This program, ZPO_XML_ALV_REPORT, demonstrates how SAP ABAP can be used to manage such hierarchical Purchase Order data through deep structures, XML serialization/deserialization, frontend file handling, and SALV ALV reporting. The solution provides two operational modes: Download and Upload. In Download mode, Purchase Order data is retrieved from the standard SAP tables EKKO and EKPO, organized into a deep structure, converted into XML using the ABAP Identity Transformation (CALL TRANSFORMATION ID), and downloaded as an XML file. In Upload mode, an existing XML file is selected from the frontend, converted back into the corresponding ABAP deep structure, and processed for display.

Since hierarchical deep structures are not directly suited for conventional ALV presentation, the program also demonstrates how the data can be flattened into an ALV-specific structure. The resulting data is displayed using CL_SALV_TABLE, providing standard ALV functionality such as optimized columns and toolbar operations.

Overall, the program illustrates a practical approach to integrating hierarchical ABAP data structures with XML-based file exchange and interactive ALV reporting, while maintaining a clear separation between data processing, file handling, transformation, and presentation.

 

Overview: ABAP Deep Structures, XML Serialization, and SALV ALV Integration

This ABAP program, zpo_xml_alv_report, demonstrates a robust approach to handling complex hierarchical data (Purchase Orders with headers and items) using Deep Structures, serializing/deserializing them to XML via identity transformation (CALL TRANSFORMATION id), and presenting the results in an interactive SALV ALV grid.

The program supports a dual-mode workflow through a selection screen:

  • Download Mode: Fetches data from standard tables (EKKO and EKPO), packages it into a deep structure, serializes it to an XML file, downloads it to the frontend, flattens the structure, and displays an ALV.

  • Upload Mode: Uploads an existing XML file from the frontend, parses/deserializes it back into a deep structure, flattens it, and displays an ALV.

Architectural Breakdown & Core Components

1. Type Declarations (Deep Structures vs. Flat Tables)

To map parent-child relationships (Header-to-Items), the program defines a nested deep structure (ty_po_deep) containing a header structure and an internal table for items:

  • ty_ekko_lite: Header fields (Purchasing Document, Company Code, Document Category, Type, Date, Created By).

  • ty_ekpo_lite: Item fields (Document, Item, Material, Short Text, Quantity, Unit, Net Price).

  • ty_po_deep: The deep structure combining header (ty_ekko_lite) and items (standard table of ty_ekpo_lite).

  • ty_alv_flat: A flattened structure combining both header and item fields, used strictly for displaying data in the ALV grid.

2. Dynamic Selection Screen (AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT)

  • Radio buttons (r_down and r_up) control whether the program runs in Download or Upload mode.

  • The USER-COMMAND cmd trigger refreshes the screen, and the LOOP AT SCREEN block dynamically hides the selection option (s_ebeln) when the user switches to Upload mode.

3. Database Selection & Deep Data Assembly (FORM get_data_from_db)

  • Header Selection: Fetches up to 100 purchase order headers from EKKO based on user input.

  • Item Selection: Uses FOR ALL ENTRIES to fetch corresponding items from EKPO.

  • Deep Nesting Logic: Loops through headers and matching items, appending them into the internal table of deep structures (lt_po_deep).

4. XML Serialization & Deserialization (ID Transformation)

  • Serialization (generate_xml Uses ABAP's built-in Identity Transformation (CALL TRANSFORMATION id SOURCE root = lt_po_deep RESULT XML lv_xml_xstring) to automatically convert the deep internal table into an XML XString format.

  • Deserialization (parse_xml Reverses the process, taking the uploaded XML XString and converting it back into the complex deep internal table format (lt_po_deep).

5. Frontend File Handling & Conversion

  • File Dialogs (f4_file_path Leverages cl_gui_frontend_services=>file_save_dialog and file_open_dialog to give users native OS window prompts.

  • Binary Conversion: Uses function modules SCMS_XSTRING_TO_BINARY and SCMS_BINARY_TO_XSTRING to bridge the gap between frontend file transfer tables (solix_tab) and backend XStrings (xstring).

6. Data Flattening & ALV Presentation

  • Flattening (prepare_alv_from_deep ALV grids cannot natively display nested internal tables. The program loops through the deep table, merges header data with each item row, and populates a flat ALV table (lt_alv).

  • SALV Model (display_alv Utilizes cl_salv_table=>factory for modern object-oriented ALV display, automatically optimizing column widths and enabling standard toolbar functions.

REPORT zpo_xml_alv_report.

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_ekpo_lite,
         ebeln TYPE ekpo-ebeln,
         ebelp TYPE ekpo-ebelp,
         matnr TYPE ekpo-matnr,
         txz01 TYPE ekpo-txz01,
         menge TYPE ekpo-menge,
         meins TYPE ekpo-meins,
         netpr TYPE ekpo-netpr,
       END OF ty_ekpo_lite.

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_ekko_lite,
         ebeln TYPE ekko-ebeln,
         bukrs TYPE ekko-bukrs,
         bstyp TYPE ekko-bstyp,
         bsart TYPE ekko-bsart,
         aedat TYPE ekko-aedat,
         ernam TYPE ekko-ernam,
       END OF ty_ekko_lite.

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_po_deep,
         header TYPE ty_ekko_lite,
         items  TYPE TABLE OF ty_ekpo_lite WITH DEFAULT KEY,
       END OF ty_po_deep.

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_alv_flat,
         ebeln TYPE ekko-ebeln,
         bukrs TYPE ekko-bukrs,
         aedat TYPE ekko-aedat,
         ebelp TYPE ekpo-ebelp,
         matnr TYPE ekpo-matnr,
         txz01 TYPE ekpo-txz01,
         menge TYPE ekpo-menge,
         netpr TYPE ekpo-netpr,
       END OF ty_alv_flat.

DATA: lt_po_deep     TYPE TABLE OF ty_po_deep,
      ls_po_deep     TYPE ty_po_deep,
      lt_alv         TYPE TABLE OF ty_alv_flat,
      ls_alv         TYPE ty_alv_flat,
      lv_xml_xstring TYPE xstring.

SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b1 WITH FRAME TITLE text-001.
  PARAMETERS: r_down RADIOBUTTON GROUP g1 DEFAULT 'X' USER-COMMAND cmd,
              r_up   RADIOBUTTON GROUP g1.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b1.

SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b2 WITH FRAME TITLE text-002.
  SELECT-OPTIONS: s_ebeln FOR ls_alv-ebeln MODIF ID dwn.
  PARAMETERS: p_file TYPE string LOWER CASE.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b2.

AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT.
  LOOP AT SCREEN.
    IF r_up = 'X' AND screen-group1 = 'DWN'.
      screen-active = 0.
    ENDIF.
    MODIFY SCREEN.
  ENDLOOP.

AT SELECTION-SCREEN ON VALUE-REQUEST FOR p_file.
  PERFORM f4_file_path CHANGING p_file.

START-OF-SELECTION.

  IF r_down = 'X'.
    PERFORM get_data_from_db.
    PERFORM generate_xml.
    PERFORM download_xml.
    PERFORM prepare_alv_from_deep.
  ELSE.
    PERFORM upload_xml.
    PERFORM parse_xml.
    PERFORM prepare_alv_from_deep.
  ENDIF.

  PERFORM display_alv.

FORM get_data_from_db.
  DATA: lt_ekko TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_ekko_lite,
        lt_ekpo TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_ekpo_lite,
        ls_ekko TYPE ty_ekko_lite,
        ls_ekpo TYPE ty_ekpo_lite.

  SELECT ebeln bukrs bstyp bsart aedat ernam
    FROM ekko
    INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF TABLE lt_ekko
    UP TO 100 ROWS
    WHERE ebeln IN s_ebeln.

  IF lt_ekko IS INITIAL.
    MESSAGE 'No data found.' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'E'.
    LEAVE LIST-PROCESSING.
  ENDIF.

  SELECT ebeln ebelp matnr txz01 menge meins netpr
    FROM ekpo
    INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF TABLE lt_ekpo
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN lt_ekko
    WHERE ebeln = lt_ekko-ebeln.

  REFRESH lt_po_deep.
  SORT lt_ekpo BY ebeln ebelp.

  LOOP AT lt_ekko INTO ls_ekko.
    CLEAR ls_po_deep.
    ls_po_deep-header = ls_ekko.
    LOOP AT lt_ekpo INTO ls_ekpo WHERE ebeln = ls_ekko-ebeln.
      APPEND ls_ekpo TO ls_po_deep-items.
    ENDLOOP.
    APPEND ls_po_deep TO lt_po_deep.
  ENDLOOP.

  MESSAGE 'Data retrieved from DB.' TYPE 'S'.
ENDFORM.

FORM generate_xml.
  TRY.
      CALL TRANSFORMATION id
        SOURCE root = lt_po_deep
        RESULT XML lv_xml_xstring.
    CATCH cx_xslt_exception INTO DATA(lx_error).
      MESSAGE lx_error->get_text( ) TYPE 'E'.
  ENDTRY.
ENDFORM.

FORM download_xml.
  DATA: lt_binary TYPE solix_tab,
        lv_length TYPE i.

  IF p_file IS INITIAL.
    MESSAGE 'Please select a file path' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'E'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  CALL FUNCTION 'SCMS_XSTRING_TO_BINARY'
    EXPORTING
      buffer        = lv_xml_xstring
    IMPORTING
      output_length = lv_length
    TABLES
      binary_tab    = lt_binary.

  cl_gui_frontend_services=>gui_download(
    EXPORTING
      bin_filesize = lv_length
      filename     = p_file
      filetype     = 'BIN'
    CHANGING
      data_tab     = lt_binary
    EXCEPTIONS
      OTHERS       = 1 ).

  IF sy-subrc = 0.
    MESSAGE 'XML Downloaded successfully' TYPE 'S'.
  ELSE.
    MESSAGE 'Error downloading file' TYPE 'E'.
  ENDIF.
ENDFORM.

FORM upload_xml.
  DATA: lt_binary TYPE solix_tab,
        lv_length TYPE i.

  IF p_file IS INITIAL.
    MESSAGE 'Please select a file path' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'E'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  cl_gui_frontend_services=>gui_upload(
    EXPORTING
      filename   = p_file
      filetype   = 'BIN'
    IMPORTING
      filelength = lv_length
    CHANGING
      data_tab   = lt_binary
    EXCEPTIONS
      OTHERS     = 1 ).

  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    MESSAGE 'Error uploading file' TYPE 'E'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  CALL FUNCTION 'SCMS_BINARY_TO_XSTRING'
    EXPORTING
      input_length = lv_length
    IMPORTING
      buffer       = lv_xml_xstring
    TABLES
      binary_tab   = lt_binary.
ENDFORM.

FORM parse_xml.
  REFRESH lt_po_deep.

  TRY.
      CALL TRANSFORMATION id
        SOURCE XML lv_xml_xstring
        RESULT root = lt_po_deep.
      MESSAGE 'XML Parsed successfully' TYPE 'S'.
    CATCH cx_xslt_exception INTO DATA(lx_error).
      MESSAGE 'XML Parsing Failed. Format mismatch?' TYPE 'E'.
  ENDTRY.
ENDFORM.

FORM prepare_alv_from_deep.
  DATA ls_ekpo TYPE ty_ekpo_lite.

  REFRESH lt_alv.

  LOOP AT lt_po_deep INTO ls_po_deep.
    IF ls_po_deep-items IS INITIAL.
      CLEAR ls_alv.
      MOVE-CORRESPONDING ls_po_deep-header TO ls_alv.
      APPEND ls_alv TO lt_alv.
    ELSE.
      LOOP AT ls_po_deep-items INTO ls_ekpo.
        CLEAR ls_alv.
        MOVE-CORRESPONDING ls_po_deep-header TO ls_alv.
        MOVE-CORRESPONDING ls_ekpo TO ls_alv.
        APPEND ls_alv TO lt_alv.
      ENDLOOP.
    ENDIF.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDFORM.

FORM display_alv.
  DATA lo_alv TYPE REF TO cl_salv_table.

  IF lt_alv IS INITIAL.
    MESSAGE 'No data to display' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'W'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  TRY.
      cl_salv_table=>factory(
        IMPORTING
          r_salv_table = lo_alv
        CHANGING
          t_table      = lt_alv ).

      lo_alv->get_columns( )->set_optimize( 'X' ).
      lo_alv->get_functions( )->set_all( 'X' ).
      lo_alv->display( ).

    CATCH cx_salv_msg.
      MESSAGE 'Error displaying ALV' TYPE 'E'.
  ENDTRY.
ENDFORM.

FORM f4_file_path CHANGING cv_file TYPE string.
  DATA: lt_file_table TYPE filetable,
        ls_file       TYPE file_table,
        lv_rc         TYPE i,
        lv_filename   TYPE string,
        lv_path       TYPE string,
        lv_fullpath   TYPE string.

  IF r_down = 'X'.
    cl_gui_frontend_services=>file_save_dialog(
      EXPORTING
        window_title      = 'Save XML File'
        default_extension = 'xml'
        file_filter       = '*.xml'
      CHANGING
        filename          = lv_filename
        path              = lv_path
        fullpath          = lv_fullpath ).

    IF lv_fullpath IS NOT INITIAL.
      cv_file = lv_fullpath.
    ENDIF.
  ELSE.
    cl_gui_frontend_services=>file_open_dialog(
      EXPORTING
        window_title      = 'Select XML File'
        default_extension = 'xml'
        file_filter       = '*.xml'
      CHANGING
        file_table        = lt_file_table
        rc                = lv_rc ).

    READ TABLE lt_file_table INTO ls_file INDEX 1.
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      cv_file = ls_file-filename.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.
ENDFORM.

Key Takeaways

  • Simplicity of Identity Transformations: Using CALL TRANSFORMATION ID eliminates the need to write custom XSLT style sheets or explicit serialization loops.

  • Separation of Concerns: Deep structures excel at hierarchical business logic representations, whereas flat structures are necessary for UI outputs like standard ALV grids.

Conclusion:

The ZPO_XML_ALV_REPORT program provides a simple and effective demonstration of how complex Purchase Order data can be handled in SAP ABAP using deep structures and XML processing. By combining header and item information into a hierarchical structure, the program preserves the natural parent-child relationship of Purchase Order data.

The use of CALL TRANSFORMATION ID significantly simplifies XML serialization and deserialization by allowing ABAP structures to be converted to XML and restored without requiring a custom transformation stylesheet. The frontend file handling functionality further enables users to easily download generated XML files or upload existing XML files for processing.

The program also highlights the importance of separating the business data model from the presentation model. While deep structures are well suited for representing hierarchical data, the flattened structure provides an appropriate format for displaying the information in a SALV ALV grid. This separation makes the solution easier to understand, maintain, and extend.

In conclusion, this approach demonstrates how ABAP deep structures, XML file exchange, frontend services, and SALV ALV can work together to build a reusable solution for hierarchical business data. The same design can be extended to other SAP scenarios involving parent-child relationships and XML-based data integration, making it a useful pattern for practical ABAP development.

entry.title: Securing Draft Data in SAP RAP with Draft Query Views
entry.content:
Introduction  

The Draft capability in SAP RAP allows users to create, edit, and save business data without immediately changing the active business data.    

This is what powers the familiar Draft behavior in Fiori Elements applications. For example, a user can start filling in a form, navigate away, and later return to continue working on it — all before the data is finally activated as an active business record.    

Under the hood, RAP stores draft instances in a separate draft persistence (draft table), which is managed by the RAP framework.    

This introduces an important consideration when implementing access control. DCL (Data Control Language) is defined on CDS views, not directly on database tables. Also, access restrictions defined for the active CDS view do not automatically restrict access to draft instances.    

To address this requirement, SAP RAP provides the Draft Query View — a CDS view built on top of the draft table and connected to the behavior definition using the query addition.    

Once the Draft Query View is assigned, RAP can use this CDS view when querying draft instances. This provides a CDS-based layer where access restrictions can be defined specifically for draft data.    

In this blog, I'll walk through building a Price Change Request application end-to-end and demonstrate how the Draft Query View can be used to control access to draft instances.    

Why Does Draft Data Need Special Handling?    

A Draft Query View is a CDS view that reads data from the draft persistence.    

By default, DCL access restrictions defined for the active CDS view entity do not automatically apply to draft data. Draft instances therefore require their own access-control consideration.    

By assigning a Draft Query View using the query addition in the behavior definition, RAP can use the CDS view when reading draft instances. This allows you to define purpose-built access restrictions for draft data, similar to how access control is defined for active data.   

Implementation steps 

Step 1 : Create  a Data Base Table 

@EndUserText.label : 'Price Change Request'
@AbapCatalog.enhancement.category : #NOT_EXTENSIBLE
@AbapCatalog.tableCategory : #TRANSPARENT
@AbapCatalog.deliveryClass : #A
@AbapCatalog.dataMaintenance : #RESTRICTED
define table zaf_dt_pricerequ {

  key client     : abap.clnt not null;
  key request_id : abap.char(10) not null;
  material       : abap.char(18);
  sales_org      : abap.char(4);
  customer       : abap.char(10);
  current_price  : abap.dec(15,2);
  new_price      : abap.dec(15,2);
  currency       : abap.cuky;
  valid_from     : abap.dats;
  reason         : abap.char(90);
  status         : abap.char(20);
  changed_at     : timestampl;
  changed_by     : abap.char(15);
  created_at     : timestampl;
  created_by     : abap.char(15);

}

Step 2 : Create root CDS view for table

@AbapCatalog.viewEnhancementCategory: [#NONE]
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #CHECK
@EndUserText.label: 'Price Change Request'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true
define root view entity ZAF_I_PRICEREQU as select from zaf_dt_pricerequ
{
    key request_id as RequestId,
    material as Material,
    sales_org as SalesOrg,
    customer as Customer,
    current_price as CurrentPrice,
    new_price as NewPrice,
    currency as Currency,
    valid_from as ValidFrom,
    reason as Reason,
    status as Status,
    @Semantics.systemDateTime.lastChangedAt: true
    changed_at as ChangedAt,
    changed_by as ChangedBy,
    created_at as CreatedAt,
    created_by as CreatedBy
}

Step 3: create projection view

@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #CHECK
@EndUserText.label: 'Projection View'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true
@Metadata.allowExtensions: true
define root view entity ZAF_C_PRICEREQDF 
provider contract transactional_query
as projection on ZAF_I_PRICEREQU
{
    key RequestId,
    Material,
    SalesOrg,
    Customer,
    CurrentPrice,
    NewPrice,
    Currency,
    ValidFrom,
    Reason,
    Status,
    ChangedAt,
    ChangedBy,
    CreatedAt,
    CreatedBy
}

Step 4: Create the Projection Behavior Definition

projection;
strict ( 2 );
use draft;

define behavior for ZAF_C_PRICEREQDF 
{
  use create;
  use update;
  use delete;

  use action Activate;
  use action Discard;
  use action Edit;
  use action Resume;
  use action Prepare;
}


Step 5: Create Metadata Extension

@Metadata.layer: #CORE
annotate entity ZAF_C_PRICEREQDF
  with
{
  @UI.facet: [
    {
      id: 'PriceRequestHeader',
      purpose: #STANDARD,
      type: #IDENTIFICATION_REFERENCE,
      label: 'Price Change Request Details',
      position: 10
    }
  ]

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 10, label: 'Request ID' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 10, label: 'Request ID' } ]
  RequestId;

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 20, label: 'Material' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 20, label: 'Material' } ]
  Material;

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 30, label: 'Sales Organization' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 30, label: 'Sales Organization' } ]
  SalesOrg;

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 40, label: 'Customer' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 40, label: 'Customer' } ]
  Customer;

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 50, label: 'Current Price' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 50, label: 'Current Price' } ]
  CurrentPrice;

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 60, label: 'New Price' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 60, label: 'New Price' } ]
  NewPrice;

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 70, label: 'Currency' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 70, label: 'Currency' } ]
  Currency;

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 80, label: 'Valid From' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 80, label: 'Valid From' } ]
  ValidFrom;

  @UI.lineItem: [ { position: 90, label: 'Status' } ]
  @UI.identification: [ { position: 90, label: 'Status' } ]
  Status;

  @UI.identification: [ { position: 100, label: 'Reason' } ]
  Reason;

  @UI.hidden: true
  ChangedAt;
  @UI.hidden: true
  ChangedBy;
  @UI.hidden: true
  CreatedAt;
  @UI.hidden: true
  CreatedBy;
}

Step 6:  Create Behavior Definition 

  • Create the Draft Table.  
  • After creating the Draft Table, create an Interface CDS View on top of the Draft Table.  
  • In the behavior definition, declare the Draft Table using the query keyword and provide the name of the Interface CDS View created on top of the Draft Table. 

A few important points about this definition:  

  • Draft table zaf_df_pricedf query ZAF_I_PRICEREQUDF is the key line for this entire blog — it declares the draft table AND assigns the draft query view that will secure it. 

Step 7: Create Draft Data Base Table

@EndUserText.label : 'Draft table for entity ZAF_I_PRICEREQU'
@AbapCatalog.enhancement.category : #EXTENSIBLE_ANY
@AbapCatalog.tableCategory : #TRANSPARENT
@AbapCatalog.deliveryClass : #A
@AbapCatalog.dataMaintenance : #RESTRICTED
define table zaf_df_pricedf {

  key mandt     : mandt not null;
  key requestid : abap.char(10) not null;
  material      : abap.char(18);
  salesorg      : abap.char(4);
  customer      : abap.char(10);
  currentprice  : abap.dec(15,2);
  newprice      : abap.dec(15,2);
  currency      : abap.cuky;
  validfrom     : abap.dats;
  reason        : abap.char(90);
  status        : abap.char(20);
  changedat     : timestampl;
  changedby     : abap.char(15);
  createdat     : timestampl;
  createdby     : abap.char(15);
  "%admin"      : include sych_bdl_draft_admin_inc;

}

Step 8: Interface view of Draft data base table

@AbapCatalog.viewEnhancementCategory: [#NONE]
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #CHECK
@EndUserText.label: 'View on draft table'
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true
define view entity ZAF_I_PRICEREQUDF
  as select from zaf_df_pricedf
  association [0..1] to I_DraftAdministrativeData as _DraftAdminData
    on $projection.DraftAdministrativeDataUUID = _DraftAdminData.DraftUUID
{
    key requestid                       as Requestid,
    material                            as Material,
    salesorg                            as Salesorg,
    customer                            as Customer,
    currentprice                        as Currentprice,
    newprice                            as Newprice,
    currency                            as Currency,
    validfrom                           as Validfrom,
    reason                              as Reason,
    status                              as Status,
    changedat                           as Changedat,
    changedby                           as Changedby,
    createdat                           as Createdat,
    createdby                           as Createdby,
    draftentitycreationdatetime         as Draftentitycreationdatetime,
    draftentitylastchangedatetime       as Draftentitylastchangedatetime,
    draftadministrativedatauuid         as DraftAdministrativeDataUUID,
    draftentityoperationcode            as Draftentityoperationcode,
    hasactiveentity                     as Hasactiveentity,
    draftfieldchanges                   as Draftfieldchanges,
    _DraftAdminData.InProcessByUser     as InProcessByUser,
    _DraftAdminData
}

Step 9: Create the DCL Roles

Two separate DCL roles are needed — one for the active view, one for the draft query view. 

Active data access control:

@EndUserText.label: 'Access control for price request active'
@MappingRole: true
define role ZAF_DCL_PRICEREQU {
    grant
        select
            on
                ZAF_I_PRICEREQU
                    where
                        Createdby = aspect user;

}

Draft data access control:

@EndUserText.label: 'Access control for price request draft'
@MappingRole: true
define role ZAF_DCL_PRICEREQU_DF {
    grant
        select
            on
                ZAF_I_PRICEREQUDF
               where
                        InProcessByUser = aspect user;
}

Notice these two roles filter on different fields — Createdby for active data, but InProcessByUser for draft data. This isn't arbitrary; it comes down to when each field actually gets populated.  

When a user clicks Create, RAP immediately and automatically inserts a row into the draft table — before any custom ABAP code runs. At that exact moment, the framework populates the draft admin data (including InProcessByUser, accessible via the association to I_DraftAdministrativeData), because that's system-managed data the framework itself owns.  

Createdby, on the other hand, is a business field — it only gets a value inside the handler class's create method, which only executes later, when Activate/Save is triggered. So immediately after Create, Createdby on the draft table is still blank, and filtering on it would silently hide every newly created draft.  

The rule of thumb: filter draft data using framework-populated draft admin fields, and filter active data using your own business fields — by the time something is active, your own logic has already run and populated them correctly. 

Step 10: Create the Behavior Handler and Saver Classes

CLASS lhc_ZAF_I_PRICEREQU DEFINITION
  INHERITING FROM cl_abap_behavior_handler.

  PRIVATE SECTION.

    METHODS get_instance_authorizations
      FOR INSTANCE AUTHORIZATION
      IMPORTING
                keys REQUEST requested_authorizations
                  FOR zaf_i_pricerequ
      RESULT    result.

    METHODS create
      FOR MODIFY
      IMPORTING entities FOR CREATE zaf_i_pricerequ.

    METHODS earlynumbering_create
      FOR NUMBERING
      IMPORTING entities FOR CREATE zaf_i_pricerequ.

    METHODS update
      FOR MODIFY
      IMPORTING entities FOR UPDATE zaf_i_pricerequ.

    METHODS delete
      FOR MODIFY
      IMPORTING keys FOR DELETE zaf_i_pricerequ.

    METHODS read
      FOR READ
      IMPORTING keys   FOR READ zaf_i_pricerequ
      RESULT    result.

    METHODS lock
      FOR LOCK
      IMPORTING keys FOR LOCK zaf_i_pricerequ.

ENDCLASS.


CLASS lhc_ZAF_I_PRICEREQU IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD get_instance_authorizations.

    result = VALUE #(
      FOR key IN keys
      ( %tky    = key-%tky
        %update = if_abap_behv=>auth-allowed
        %delete = if_abap_behv=>auth-allowed ) ).

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD earlynumbering_create.

    DATA:
      lv_max_active TYPE i,
      lv_max_draft  TYPE i,
      lv_max_id     TYPE i,
      lv_new_id     TYPE zaf_dt_pricerequ-request_id.

    SELECT MAX( request_id )
      FROM zaf_dt_pricerequ
      INTO @DATA(lv_ext_active).

    IF lv_ext_active IS NOT INITIAL.
      lv_max_active = CONV i( lv_ext_active+2 ).
    ENDIF.

    SELECT MAX( requestid )
      FROM zaf_df_pricedf
      INTO @DATA(lv_ext_draft).

    IF lv_ext_draft IS NOT INITIAL.
      lv_max_draft = CONV i( lv_ext_draft+2 ).
    ENDIF.

    lv_max_id = nmax( val1 = lv_max_active val2 = lv_max_draft ).

    IF lv_max_id < 100010.
      lv_max_id = 100010.
    ENDIF.

    LOOP AT entities ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_entity>).

      IF <fs_entity>-RequestId IS NOT INITIAL.

        lv_new_id = <fs_entity>-RequestId.

      ELSE.

        WHILE 1 = 1.
          lv_max_id += 1.
          lv_new_id = |PR{ lv_max_id }|.

          SELECT SINGLE request_id FROM zaf_dt_pricerequ WHERE request_id = @LV_new_id INTO @DATA(lv_check_act).
          SELECT SINGLE requestid FROM zaf_df_pricedf WHERE requestid = @LV_new_id INTO @DATA(lv_check_dft).

          IF lv_check_act IS INITIAL AND lv_check_dft IS INITIAL.
            EXIT.
          ENDIF.
        ENDWHILE.

      ENDIF.

      APPEND VALUE #(
        %cid      = <fs_entity>-%cid
        RequestId = lv_new_id
        %is_draft = <fs_entity>-%is_draft
      ) TO mapped-zaf_i_pricerequ.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD create.

    zcl_af_pricerequ=>get_instance( )->create_data(
      EXPORTING
        entities = entities
      CHANGING
        mapped   = mapped
        failed   = failed
        reported = reported ).

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD update.

    zcl_af_pricerequ=>get_instance( )->update_data(
      EXPORTING
        entities = entities
      CHANGING
        mapped   = mapped
        failed   = failed
        reported = reported ).

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD delete.

    zcl_af_pricerequ=>get_instance( )->delete_data(
      EXPORTING
        keys = keys
      CHANGING
        mapped   = mapped
        failed   = failed
        reported = reported ).

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD read.

    zcl_af_pricerequ=>get_instance( )->read_data(
      EXPORTING
        keys = keys
      CHANGING
        result   = result
        failed   = failed
        reported = reported ).

  ENDMETHOD.


METHOD lock.

ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.


CLASS lsc_ZAF_I_PRICEREQU DEFINITION
  INHERITING FROM cl_abap_behavior_saver.

  PROTECTED SECTION.

    METHODS finalize REDEFINITION.
    METHODS check_before_save REDEFINITION.
    METHODS save REDEFINITION.
    METHODS cleanup REDEFINITION.
    METHODS cleanup_finalize REDEFINITION.

ENDCLASS.


CLASS lsc_ZAF_I_PRICEREQU IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD finalize.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD check_before_save.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD save.

    zcl_af_pricerequ=>get_instance( )->save_data( ).

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD cleanup.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD cleanup_finalize.
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

Step 11: Create the Helper Class

CLASS zcl_af_pricerequ DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.

    TYPES:
      tt_create   TYPE TABLE FOR CREATE zaf_i_pricerequ,
      tt_update   TYPE TABLE FOR UPDATE zaf_i_pricerequ,
      tt_delete   TYPE TABLE FOR DELETE zaf_i_pricerequ,
      tt_read     TYPE TABLE FOR READ IMPORT zaf_i_pricerequ,
      tt_result   TYPE TABLE FOR READ RESULT zaf_i_pricerequ,

      tt_mapped   TYPE RESPONSE FOR MAPPED zaf_i_pricerequ,
      tt_failed   TYPE RESPONSE FOR FAILED zaf_i_pricerequ,
      tt_reported TYPE RESPONSE FOR REPORTED zaf_i_pricerequ.

    CLASS-METHODS get_instance
      RETURNING VALUE(ro_instance) TYPE REF TO zcl_af_pricerequ.

    METHODS create_data
      IMPORTING
        entities TYPE tt_create
      CHANGING
        mapped   TYPE tt_mapped
        failed   TYPE tt_failed
        reported TYPE tt_reported.

    METHODS update_data
      IMPORTING
        entities TYPE tt_update
      CHANGING
        mapped   TYPE tt_mapped
        failed   TYPE tt_failed
        reported TYPE tt_reported.

    METHODS delete_data
      IMPORTING
        keys     TYPE tt_delete
      CHANGING
        mapped   TYPE tt_mapped
        failed   TYPE tt_failed
        reported TYPE tt_reported.

    METHODS read_data
      IMPORTING
        keys     TYPE tt_read
      CHANGING
        result   TYPE tt_result
        failed   TYPE tt_failed
        reported TYPE tt_reported.

    METHODS save_data.

  PRIVATE SECTION.

    CLASS-DATA mo_instance TYPE REF TO zcl_af_pricerequ.

    DATA:
      mt_create TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zaf_dt_pricerequ,
      mt_update TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zaf_dt_pricerequ,
      mt_delete TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zaf_dt_pricerequ.

ENDCLASS.


CLASS zcl_af_pricerequ IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD get_instance.

    IF mo_instance IS INITIAL.
      mo_instance = NEW zcl_af_pricerequ( ).
    ENDIF.

    ro_instance = mo_instance.

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD create_data.

    DATA:
      ls_db        TYPE zaf_dt_pricerequ,
      lv_timestamp TYPE timestampl.

    GET TIME STAMP FIELD lv_timestamp.

    LOOP AT entities ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_entity>).

      CLEAR ls_db.

      ls_db = VALUE #(
        client        = sy-mandt
        request_id    = <fs_entity>-RequestId
        material      = <fs_entity>-Material
        sales_org     = <fs_entity>-SalesOrg
        customer      = <fs_entity>-Customer
        current_price = <fs_entity>-CurrentPrice
        new_price     = <fs_entity>-NewPrice
        currency      = <fs_entity>-Currency
        valid_from    = <fs_entity>-ValidFrom
        reason        = <fs_entity>-Reason
        status        = 'NEW'
        changed_at    = lv_timestamp
        changed_by    = sy-uname
        created_at    = lv_timestamp
        created_by    = sy-uname
      ).

      APPEND ls_db TO mt_create.

      APPEND VALUE #(
        %cid      = <fs_entity>-%cid
        RequestId = <fs_entity>-RequestId
        %is_draft = <fs_entity>-%is_draft
      ) TO mapped-zaf_i_pricerequ.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD update_data.

    DATA:
      ls_db        TYPE zaf_dt_pricerequ,
      lv_timestamp TYPE timestampl.

    GET TIME STAMP FIELD lv_timestamp.

    LOOP AT entities ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_entity>).

      SELECT SINGLE FROM zaf_dt_pricerequ
        FIELDS *
        WHERE request_id = @<fs_entity>-RequestId
        INTO @LS_db.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.

        APPEND VALUE #(
          %key-RequestId = <fs_entity>-RequestId
        ) TO failed-zaf_i_pricerequ.

        CONTINUE.

      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-Material = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-material = <fs_entity>-Material.
      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-SalesOrg = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-sales_org = <fs_entity>-SalesOrg.
      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-Customer = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-customer = <fs_entity>-Customer.
      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-CurrentPrice = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-current_price = <fs_entity>-CurrentPrice.
      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-NewPrice = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-new_price = <fs_entity>-NewPrice.
      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-Currency = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-currency = <fs_entity>-Currency.
      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-ValidFrom = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-valid_from = <fs_entity>-ValidFrom.
      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-Reason = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-reason = <fs_entity>-Reason.
      ENDIF.

      IF <fs_entity>-%control-Status = if_abap_behv=>mk-on.
        ls_db-status = <fs_entity>-Status.
      ENDIF.

      ls_db-changed_at = lv_timestamp.
      ls_db-changed_by = sy-uname.

      APPEND ls_db TO mt_update.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD delete_data.

    LOOP AT keys ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_key>).

      SELECT SINGLE request_id
        FROM zaf_dt_pricerequ
        WHERE request_id = @<fs_key>-RequestId
        INTO @DATA(lv_request_id).

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.

        APPEND VALUE #(
          %key-RequestId = <fs_key>-RequestId
        ) TO failed-zaf_i_pricerequ.

        CONTINUE.

      ENDIF.

      APPEND VALUE #(
        client     = sy-mandt
        request_id = <fs_key>-RequestId
      ) TO mt_delete.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD read_data.

    IF keys IS INITIAL.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    SELECT
      RequestId,
      Material,
      SalesOrg,
      Customer,
      CurrentPrice,
      NewPrice,
      Currency,
      ValidFrom,
      Reason,
      Status,
      ChangedAt,
      ChangedBy,
      CreatedAt,
      CreatedBy
      FROM zaf_i_pricerequ
      FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @Keys
      WHERE RequestId = @Keys-RequestId
      INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF TABLE @result.

  ENDMETHOD.


  METHOD save_data.

    IF mt_create IS NOT INITIAL.
      INSERT zaf_dt_pricerequ FROM TABLE @MT_create.
    ENDIF.

    IF mt_update IS NOT INITIAL.
      UPDATE zaf_dt_pricerequ FROM TABLE @MT_update.
    ENDIF.

    IF mt_delete IS NOT INITIAL.
      DELETE zaf_dt_pricerequ FROM TABLE @MT_delete.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

Step 12: Create the Service Definition

@EndUserText.label: 'Price Change Request UI Service'
define service ZAF_SD_PRICEREQU {
  expose ZAF_C_PRICEREQDF as PriceRequest;
}

Step 13 : Create the Service Binding

The Binding Type has to be ODATA V4 

Result

User A is trying to create the record 

Fig 2 — Create Form (Draft in progress): A new Price Change Request being filled in. Request ID PR100021 is already assigned via early numbering, and the "Draft updated" message confirms the entered fields are being persisted to the draft table before the final Create button is clicked. 

Fig 3 — Draft Table Data Preview: Confirming PR100021 is correctly persisted in the draft table (zaf_df_pricedf) with every field intact — proof that the draft query view and DCL setup allow this data to be read back correctly, rather than showing up blank as in the original bug. 

Now whenever other user (User B) tries to check for the record, which is in draft table, for that User B the draft table record will not be visible. 

But for the user (User A), the record in the draft table is visible. So only User A can make changes to the record which is in the draft table.  

 

Conclusion

This blog walked through implementing a draft-enabled RAP business object for a Price Change Request scenario, with particular focus on securing draft data using a Draft Query View. 

The key takeaway is that draft-enabled RAP objects work perfectly well without a draft query view — but doing so leaves draft data effectively unprotected by DCL, since access restrictions defined on the active CDS view entity do not automatically extend to draft instances. The query addition in the behavior definition closes this gap by giving draft reads their own dedicated CDS view, which can carry its own DCL role. 

A second, less obvious lesson from this implementation: filtering draft data by "ownership" needs to use framework-managed data (via an association to I_DraftAdministrativeData), not custom business fields like CreatedBy — because business fields are only populated once your own class logic runs, which happens later than the moment the draft row is actually created. 

Together, these two points are the core of what a Draft Query View is for, and why it matters beyond just being a syntax addition in the behavior definition.
